baseline_manifest_entry.title: A first resolvent estimate does not ensure the prescribed semigroup bound
baseline_manifest_entry.statement: Let $X=\mathbb C^2$ over the complex field ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]) have the maximum product norm $\|(z_1,z_2)\|_\infty=\max(|z_1|,|z_2|)$ ([[def-product-norms-on-finitely-many-normed-spaces]], [[rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention]]); this finite-dimensional normed space is Banach ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]]). Let $A\in\mathcal B(X)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) be the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-1&4\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ with domain $D(A)=X$. For $M=25/16$ and $\omega=0$, every $\lambda>0$ lies in $\rho(A)$ and the first resolvent estimate $\|R(\lambda,A)\|_\infty\le M/\lambda$ holds ([[def-resolvent-of-a-closed-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]). But the $n=2$ Hille--Yosida estimate required by [[thm-hille-yosida-generation-theorem]] fails at $\lambda=3$: $\|R(3,A)^2\|_\infty=3/16>25/144=M/3^2$. The bounded-operator exponential semigroup generated by $A$ ([[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]]) is $e^{tA}=e^{-t}\begin{pmatrix}1&4t\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, and $\|e^{A/2}\|_\infty=3e^{-1/2}>25/16$. Thus a first-power resolvent estimate alone does not ensure the semigroup bound with the same $M>1$ and $\omega=0$.
baseline_manifest_entry.strategy: Set $N=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$, so $N^2=0$ and $A=-I+4N$. The standard matrix multiplication [[def-matrix-product-and-identity-matrix]] gives this nilpotence and the matrix powers below. By the operator-norm definition [[def-operator-norm]], the induced norm of a matrix on the maximum norm is the maximum of its absolute row sums. For $\lambda>0$, direct inversion gives $R(\lambda,A)=\begin{pmatrix}(\lambda+1)^{-1}&4(\lambda+1)^{-2}\\0&(\lambda+1)^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$, so $\lambda\|R(\lambda,A)\|_\infty=5x-4x^2=25/16-4(x-5/8)^2\le25/16$, where $x=\lambda/(\lambda+1)\in(0,1)$. At $\lambda=3$, direct multiplication gives $R=\begin{pmatrix}1/4&1/4\\0&1/4\end{pmatrix}$ and $R^2=\begin{pmatrix}1/16&1/8\\0&1/16\end{pmatrix}$; its maximum row sum is $3/16=27/144$, larger than $M/3^2=25/144$. The nilpotence of $N$ and the bounded-operator exponential result [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] give $e^{tA}=e^{-t}(I+4tN)$, whose norm is $(1+4t)e^{-t}$ for $t\ge0$. At $t=1/2$ this is $3/\sqrt e>3/\sqrt3=\sqrt3>25/16$, using $e<3$ ([[cor-two-less-than-e-less-than-three]]) and $3>(25/16)^2$. The failed second-power condition, also required by [[thm-hille-yosida-generation-theorem]], confirms that the first-power bound does not suffice for this $M>1$.

current_manifest_entry.title: A first resolvent estimate does not ensure the prescribed semigroup bound
current_manifest_entry.statement:
Assume Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $X=\mathbb C^2$ over the complex field ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]) have the maximum product norm
$$\|(z_1,z_2)\|_\infty=\max(|z_1|,|z_2|)$$
([[def-product-norms-on-finitely-many-normed-spaces]], [[rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention]]); this finite-dimensional normed space is Banach ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]]). Let $A\in\mathcal B(X)$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]) be the matrix
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}-1&4\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad D(A)=X.$$
For $M=25/16$ and $\omega=0$, every $\lambda>0$ lies in $\rho(A)$ and the first resolvent estimate
$$\|R(\lambda,A)\|_\infty\le \frac{M}{\lambda}$$
holds ([[def-resolvent-of-a-closed-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]). But the $n=2$ Hille--Yosida estimate required by [[thm-hille-yosida-generation-theorem]] fails at $\lambda=3$:
$$\|R(3,A)^2\|_\infty=\frac{3}{16}>\frac{25}{144}=\frac{M}{3^2}.$$
The bounded-operator exponential semigroup generated by $A$ ([[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]]) is
$$e^{tA}=e^{-t}\begin{pmatrix}1&4t\\0&1\end{pmatrix},$$
and
$$\|e^{A/2}\|_\infty=3e^{-1/2}>\frac{25}{16}.$$
Thus a first-power resolvent estimate alone does not ensure the semigroup bound with the same $M>1$ and $\omega=0$.

**Refuted claim.** For every $M\ge1$, a closed densely defined operator whose positive real resolvent set contains $(0,\infty)$ and satisfies only $\|R(\lambda,A)\|\le M/\lambda$ for all $\lambda>0$ necessarily generates a strongly continuous semigroup bounded by $M$.
